mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate continued accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%, with statistical significance (p<0.05) in a t-test against baseline returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in unemployment rate below 7.5% signals improving labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE crosses below 7.5% within the prior month, with p-value > 0.05 in a t-test against baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, with a Rank IC below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which increases corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of early-cycle expansion periods (as defined by INDPRO growth > 0.5% monthly) over a 3-year window, with p-value > 0.05 in a t-test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2% indicates expanding economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth above 2% fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, with a Rank IC below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate exceeding 2.5% signals rising price pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 2.5%, with p-value < 0.05 in a t-test against baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strong employment growth (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, with a Rank IC below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low interest rate environment, a stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals sustained monetary accommodation, which supports equity valuations and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains stable (within 0.1% of its current level) and below 0.5%, with p-value > 0.05 in a t-test.
